title: Algebraic stacks in setoids are algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Use the fibred groupoid conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Assume every object of $\mathcal X(T)$ has only the identity automorphism for every $S$-scheme $T$, including nonreduced schemes. Then there is an algebraic space $R/S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and an equivalence of categories fibred in groupoids $h_R\simeq\mathcal X$, where $h_R(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,R)$ is discrete. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,R)$ is naturally bijective to the set of isomorphism classes of $\mathcal X(T)$.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:h_U\to\mathcal X$ by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. The hypothesis already supplies an etale stack and a diagonal representable by algebraic spaces. Thus [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent] applies to this very atlas and shows that $\mathcal X$ has effective fppf descent for objects and fppf sheaf descent for isomorphisms. No finiteness or separation assumption on $S$ is used.

source.place: Tag 076V, lemma-stacks-etale; algebraic.tex Tag 04SZ, choice of smooth atlas.

proof.text: Two isomorphisms $a,b:x\to y$ in any fibre agree, since $b^{-1}a$ is an automorphism of $x$ and hence the identity. Put $F(T)=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal X(T))/\cong$, with restriction $[x]\mapsto[u^*x]$ along $u:T'\to T$. Cartesian pullbacks [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] are unique up to isomorphism, so these maps are well defined and obey the presheaf identities. Let $\mathcal S_F$ be its category of elements: objects are $(T,s)$, and an arrow over $u$ exists exactly when the source section is $F(u)$ of the target section. The class functor $Q:\mathcal X\to\mathcal S_F$ is fully faithful over the base: arrows over $u$ correspond to isomorphisms to the pullback along $u$, which exist exactly for equality of classes and are unique. It is essentially surjective since every class has a representative. Choosing representatives gives a quasi-inverse; uniqueness of arrows makes its compositions and comparison isomorphisms coherent.

source.place: Tag 0432, lemma-stack-in-setoids-characterize; explicit class construction and equivalence.

proof.text: The presheaf $F$ is an fppf sheaf. For a matching family $[x_i]\in F(T_i)$ on an fppf cover of $T$, equality of classes on each overlap supplies an isomorphism between the two restrictions. It is unique by step 2, so the cocycle condition holds. Effective fppf descent from [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent] gives $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ with these classes. If $[x]$ and $[y]$ agree locally, their unique local isomorphisms agree on overlaps and glue by the same cited node's fppf sheaf condition for isomorphisms. Hence $x\cong y$, proving uniqueness of the glued class. This includes the empty covering: descent gives one isomorphism class over the empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 0432, lemma-stack-in-setoids-characterize, sheaf criterion (argument written out).

proof.text: Set $q:h_U\to F$ to be $q(u)=[p(u)]$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ and $s\in F(T)$, choose $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ representing $s$. The atlas supplies an algebraic space $P_x$ equivalent over $T$ to $h_U\times_{\mathcal X}h_T$, with smooth surjective projection to $T$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. For every test $V$, objects of this 2-fibre product are triples $(u:V\to U,t:V\to T,\alpha:p(u)\cong t^*x)$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. For a fixed pair $(u,t)$ there is exactly one such $\alpha$ if $q(u)=F(t)(s)$, and none otherwise. The two scheme functors are discrete, so the triples have only identity arrows. Forgetting $\alpha$ therefore gives bijections $P_x(V)\cong(h_U\times_Fh_T)(V)$ over $h_T$; they commute with restriction, since a restricted isomorphism is again the unique one. Thus the sheaf pullback is precisely $P_x$ with its given projection.

source.place: Tag 04SZ, passage from the atlas to h_U -> F; Tags 0458 and 04TC, with the pullback comparison written explicitly.

proof.text: For every etale scheme chart $V\to P_x$, the composite $V\to T$ is smooth by the atlas convention [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] it is flat and locally of finite presentation. These are exactly the chartwise properties required of $P_x\to T$ in [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap]; its surjectivity is already that of the atlas. Regard $U$ as the algebraic space $h_U$ by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Step 3 supplies the fppf sheaf hypothesis, and step 4 supplies every scheme-test pullback. Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap] to $q:h_U\to F$: $F$ is an algebraic space over $S$. Denote it by $R$.

source.place: Tag 04SZ, final paragraph; Morphisms Tags 01VE/01VF; Bootstrap Tag 04S6, theorem-final-bootstrap (4), via the existing condition-(3) node.

proof.text: By [def-trf-algebraic-space], $R$ is the very sheaf $F$, so $\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,R)=F(T)$: a scheme as an algebraic space is its Yoneda sheaf [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], and a natural map $h_T\to F$ is determined by its value on $\mathrm{id}_T$, with inverse $s\mapsto(t\mapsto F(t)(s))$. Hence the discrete fibred groupoid $h_R$ is $\mathcal S_F$. The quasi-inverse of $Q$ from step 2 gives $h_R\simeq\mathcal X$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$. Its induced bijection with isomorphism classes is $F(T)=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal X(T))/\cong$ itself, and the restriction formula in step 2 proves naturality for every base morphism.

source.place: Tag 04SZ, conclusion (1) implies (3), and the definition of representation by an algebraic space.
